common_name: Carolina Primrose Gladiolus (Cold-Hardy Pale-Yellow Species Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant corms 4 inches deep in full sun after the danger of frost has passed; Carolina Primrose is a cold-hardy Gladiolus dalenii selection from the same hardy-hybrid breeding work that produced Boone, and like Boone it can often be left in the ground through zone 6 winters where standard hybrid gladiolus corms must be lifted.

directions: Carolina Primrose bears soft primrose-yellow flowers on a cold-hardy Gladiolus dalenii species hybrid, part of the same Southeastern hardy-gladiolus breeding effort that produced the peachy-apricot cultivar Boone. Its pale, clear yellow color and shorter, sturdier spikes than typical hybrid gladiolus make it useful for naturalizing in mixed perennial borders rather than staking in rows for cutting. Plant corms in well-drained soil in full sun, and in zones where it is winter hardy, let clumps stay in place year to year instead of digging annually; where hardiness is marginal, lift corms after foliage yellows in fall and store them cool and dry over winter. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.
